<query>I noticed the trainer at work only adjusts his broom when he’s near me, like he wants to impress me silently. Can someone’s body language really reveal feelings they won’t admit? Sometimes I feel like I’m the only one who catches these little signs of secret admiration.</query>
<response>Body language can indeed reveal unspoken emotions, as nonverbal cues like posture, eye contact, and subtle gestures often align with hidden feelings. When someone adjusts their behavior (e.g., "fixing" a broom) in your presence, it might signal nervousness, interest, or a desire to appear capable—though interpretations vary. However, context matters: cultural norms, personal habits, or situational pressures could also explain the behavior. While your observation is valid, it’s wise to avoid over-interpreting without clearer signals (e.g., consistent eye contact, mirroring actions, or verbal curiosity). If curious, consider subtle, low-pressure ways to gauge their intent—while trusting your own perception of their "secret admiration."</response>
